presentingComplaint: Three weeks of low-grade illness, tiredness and a chronic cough, referred as ?lung cancer / ?TB after an abnormal chest X-ray.
history: Warehouse worker who presented not with a dramatic febrile illness but with an insidious 3-week history of malaise, anorexia and a persistent cough now productive of moderate volumes of sputum. He and his family noticed only intermittent low-grade evening temperatures rather than swinging fevers, and drenching night sweats twice in the last week. He has lost about 5 kg unintentionally. Only on direct questioning did he admit the sputum has recently become foul-tasting/foul-smelling. Background of heavy alcohol use and poor dental hygiene with several carious teeth and periodontal disease; a witnessed episode of choking/vomiting after a drinking binge roughly 4 weeks ago. No prior TB, no known malignancy, non-diabetic. Because of the weight loss, night sweats and indolent course he was initially worked up for pulmonary TB and malignancy rather than a pyogenic abscess.
examination: Thin, mildly unwell but not toxic. Dentition poor with gingival disease and halitosis. Reduced breath sounds and coarse crepitations over the right posterior base with bronchial breathing; no clubbing. No lymphadenopathy. Cardiovascular and abdominal examination unremarkable.
imaging: Chest X-ray: thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right lower lobe (superior segment). CT thorax: 5.2 cm cavitating lesion with an internal air-fluid level and surrounding consolidation in the superior segment of the right lower lobe (dependent segment favoured by aspiration); no mediastinal mass or lobar collapse to suggest an obstructing tumour.
microbiology: Sputum Gram stain: mixed flora with abundant neutrophils. Sputum AFB smear negative x2 and CBNAAT (GeneXpert MTB/RIF) not detected. Sputum bacterial culture grew mixed anaerobic/oral flora. Blood cultures negative. Cytology on bronchial washings: no malignant cells.
finalDiagnosis: Primary (aspiration-related) anaerobic lung abscess presenting subacutely as a TB/malignancy mimic
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Lung Abscess
IDSA/ATS - Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-Acquired Pneumonia, 2019
British Thoracic Society - Management of Suppurative/Community-Acquired Lower Respiratory Tract Infection, 2009
stewardship: Infective; empiric cover targets oral anaerobes and streptococci. Guideline-concordant first-line is IV ampicillin-sulbactam (or amoxicillin-clavulanate); metronidazole monotherapy is inadequate. Prolonged course (often 4-6 weeks) guided by clinical and radiographic response, with dental source control.
contraindications: Avoid metronidazole monotherapy (fails to cover microaerophilic streptococci)
Avoid premature narrowing before anaerobic/aerobic cultures resulted
edgeCases: Foul-smelling sputum may be absent or only elicited on direct questioning, masking the diagnosis
Indolent presentation with weight loss and night sweats is frequently mislabelled as TB or lung cancer
Superior segment of lower lobe / posterior segment of upper lobe involvement points to aspiration in a supine/obtunded patient
expectedMaiK: A cavity with an air-fluid level in a dependent (aspiration-prone) segment, in a patient with poor dentition, alcohol excess and a recent aspiration event, plus foul sputum and mixed anaerobic flora, indicates a primary anaerobic lung abscess even when the course is indolent and TB/malignancy have been excluded.
expectedNextQuestions: Any witnessed aspiration, reduced consciousness, alcohol binges or swallowing difficulty?
State of dentition and periodontal disease?
Duration and change in character/smell of sputum; any haemoptysis?
TB contact, prior TB, HIV or immunosuppression?
Smoking history and features suggesting an obstructing endobronchial tumour?
expectedInvestigations: Sputum Gram stain and aerobic/anaerobic culture
Sputum AFB smear plus CBNAAT (GeneXpert) to exclude TB
Bronchoscopy with washings/cytology to exclude endobronchial obstruction and malignancy

investigations: Sputum Gram stain and anaerobic/aerobic culture
Sputum AFB smear and CBNAAT (GeneXpert MTB/RIF)

regressionAssertions: Differential must include PULMONARY_TB and cavitating lung_cancer
Empiric regimen must cover oral anaerobes and streptococci (ampicillin-sulbactam / amoxicillin-clavulanate; clindamycin if penicillin-allergic)
Must recommend AFB smear + CBNAAT to exclude TB before labelling as pyogenic abscess
